Context/Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy (ICI)-induced myositis (irMyositis) occurs in about 1% of patients treated with anti-PD1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies and can be debilitating or even fatal. We compared gene expression profiles from skeletal muscle biopsies between irMyositis patients, patients with spontaneous dermatomyositis (DM, comprising anti-Mi2-positive and anti-TIF1-γ-positive subtypes), and non-diseased controls (NDC). We used the NanoString nCounter PanCancer Immune Profiling Panel to perform differential gene expression (DGE) and pathway enrichment analyses.
Prompt: Please run GSEA of reactome pathways for each DE comparison: irMyositis vs Mi2 (DM), irMyositis vs TIF1y (DM), irMyositis vs NDC, Mi2 (DM) vs NDC, TIF1y (DM) vs NDC).  Then, discuss the results, highlighting any differences seen in active immunological pathways.  Focus on differences betwen irMyositis and DM.

— Analysis (focusing on irMyositis vs DM)  
• Both irMyositis vs Mi2 and vs TIF1-γ show strong **downregulation of type I and II interferon signaling** (e.g. Interferon Alpha Beta Signaling NES≈–3.9 and –3.9; Interferon Signaling NES≈–3.19 and –3.68), whereas Mi2 vs NDC and TIF1-γ vs NDC exhibit **robust upregulation** of these same modules (NES +4.99 and +4.71).  
• In irMyositis, interferon‐stimulated antiviral pathways (ISG15 antiviral mechanism, antiviral mechanism by IFN-stim genes) are **suppressed** relative to both DM subtypes.  
• Conversely, irMyositis vs Mi2 shows selective **activation** of TNF‐receptor binding (TNFs Bind Their Physiological Receptors) and **early TCR signaling** (Phosphorylation of CD3/TCR ζ chains) suggesting a shift from interferon-driven innate to TNF/T-cell receptor–mediated signaling.  
• IrMyositis vs TIF1-γ reveals heightened **adaptive immune system** and **CD28 costimulation** signatures (NES +4.50 and +3.15) that are not seen in Mi2 comparisons, indicating increased checkpoint‐ and costimulatory‐mediated T‐cell activation in irMyositis relative to TIF1-γ DM.  
• DM subtypes (Mi2, TIF1-γ) vs NDC share broad upregulation of interferon, antigen presentation, and TLR cascades—features **blunted** in irMyositis when directly contrasted to DM.  

**Key insight:** irMyositis muscle exhibits a **dampened interferon/antiviral** program but a **relative gain** in **TNF/TCR costimulatory** pathways compared to spontaneous DM, suggesting divergent immune-activation axes that may underlie ICI toxicity versus idiopathic autoimmunity.
